title: Installing an Industrial Kitchen Faucet: Replacing an Old Faucet with a Benchmarked Industrial-Style Fixture

locations.name: Under kitchen sink (probable)
locations.basis: Transcript centers on installing/removing plumbing fixtures beneath a sink; no explicit filming location

summary: This Old House guides viewers through removing an older, leaky faucet and replacing it with a single-hole industrial-style faucet designed for a multi-hole sink. The episode covers initial assessment and style rationale, shutting off water supply, using a basin wrench to loosen hard-to-reach nuts, removing the old faucet, choosing a deck plate to cover extra faucet holes, routing and connecting supply lines through a tight shank, mounting the new faucet with rubber washer, metal gasket, and a mounting yoke, orienting the handle, and finally restoring water flow to test the fixture and demonstrate the spray modes.

sections.title: Intro and design intent
sections.description: The host identifies an aging faucet with a leaky nozzle and spray hose and explains a preference for an industrial look to match a more utilitarian kitchen design. This establishes the motivation for replacement with a commercial-style faucet.

sections.title: Turn off water supply
concepts: shutting off cold and hot supplies
sections.description: The water supply lines are shut off under the sink; a faucet is opened to ensure the lines are drained before removal begins.

sections.title: Remove old faucet using basin wrench
sections.description: Because the nuts are in a cramped location, a basin wrench is employed to loosen the faucet mounting nut and free the old faucet from the sink.

sections.title: Old faucet removal complete; preparing for new faucet
sections.description: The old faucet is removed; the sink shows four holes, but the new single-hole faucet will use a deck plate to cover the extra holes. A soap dispenser is also noted as part of the new fixture.

sections.title: Attach water supply and position components
sections.description: The supply lines must be fed through a tight shank and connected to the faucet body. The installer guides a secure threading by staying straight and aligned to prevent cross-threading.

sections.title: Mounting hardware under the sink
sections.description: A rubber washer, metal gasket, and yoke with screws are positioned under the sink. Screws are threaded and tightened to compress the assembly against the sink for a secure hold.

sections.title: Install faucet through sink and finalize orientation
sections.description: The faucet shank is passed through the sink hole, then oriented and held in place as the installer completes the underside connections and aligns the handle position.

sections.title: Restore water, test flow, and demonstrate spray mode
sections.description: Water is turned back on, and the faucet is tested. The operator demonstrates the spray modes (stream vs. shower) to confirm proper operation and performance.

sections.title: Closing
sections.description: Music plays as the segment closes, signaling completion of the installation and the new industrial faucet in operation.

featured_techniques.technique: Basin wrench used to loosen faucet nut in tight space
Deck plate to cover extra faucet holes on a multi-hole sink
Fish/guide supply lines through tight shank and align threads
Ensure straight threading to avoid cross-threading when connecting supply lines
Assemble rubber washer, metal gasket, and mounting yoke under sink; secure with screws
Adjust faucet orientation and handle alignment before final tightening
Test water flow and demonstrate spray modes (stream vs shower) after install
Use of a deck plate to adapt a single-hole faucet to a multi-hole sink
Proper routing and securing of supply lines to avoid kinks/bends
